informative-css-background-image: A picture carrying real meaning (a price banner, a 'SOLD OUT' stamp) is painted via CSS background-image with no DOM text, so a screen-reader user never learns it.
meaningful-image-suppressed-as-decorativ: An image that carries needed information (a 'Verified seller' badge, a recipe-step diagram) is wrongly tagged decorative with empty alt, so a screen reader skips it.
alt-not-an-alternative-filename-placehol: An image's alt text is just a filename or junk placeholder like 'DSC_0481' or 'image', so it passes checks but tells a blind user nothing.
context-and-function-dependent-equivalen: An image's alt names what it depicts but ignores its job, so a printer-icon button reads 'inkjet printer' instead of 'Print', confusing a screen-reader user.
complex-image-long-description-incomplet: A chart, map, or diagram has alt text that sounds descriptive but omits key data it shows (the trend, the addresses), so a blind user gets only part.
image-of-text-alt-omits-the-text: An image whose content is really words (a quote graphic, a coupon banner) has alt that summarizes rather than repeating them, so a screen-reader user misses the text.
text-lookalike-glyph-substitution: Visible 'text' is secretly built from look-alike letters of another alphabet, so it reads fine by eye but a screen reader announces garbled nonsense or silence.
